title: Label-free mass spectrometry analysis of laminin with induced oxidations and chlorination’s facilitated with hypochlorous acid and myeloperoxidase treatments.
projectDescription: Basement membranes are specialized extracellular matrices that underlie arterial wall endothelial cells, with laminin being a key structural and biologically-active component. Hypochlorous acid (HOCl), a potent oxidizing and chlorinating agent, is formed in vivo at sites of inflammation, via the enzymatic action of myeloperoxidase (MPO), released by activated leukocytes. Murine Laminin was treated with two oxidative systems to mimic the exposure of MPO-derived HOCl in atherosclerotic condition.  Sites of oxidation and chlorination on isolated laminin-111 were detected and quantified by mass spectrometry. An increased number of modifications was detected with increasing oxidant exposure. HOCl oxidised 30 (of 56 total) Met and 7 (of 24) Trp-residues and chlorinated 33 (of 99) Tyr-residues; three Tyr-residues were dichlorinated. An additional 8 Met- and 10 Trp-oxidations, 14 chlorinations, and 18 dichlorinations were detected on Tyr-residues with the MPO system when compared to reagent HOCl. These data indicate that laminin is extensively modified by MPO-derived oxidants, with structural and functional changes. These modifications, and compromised cell-matrix interactions, may promote endothelial cell dysfunction, weaken the structure of atherosclerotic lesions, and enhance lesion rupture.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The extracellular matrix protein: The experiments are performed on the recombinant protein Murine laminin-111, which was purchased from Sigma Aldrich.  Treatment and sample preparation: 100 µg protein were treated with two oxidative systems. The HOCl treatment was carried out in three concentrations 0, 100, and 500 µM. For each HOCl condition four biological replicates were prepared. Three biological replicates were prepared for the enzymatic system, the treatment was carried out by addition of 500 µM H2O2, 0.1 µM MPO, and 100 mM NaCl. The experiment had three controls omitting H2O2, MPO or NaCl, as well as a control of untreated protein. The oxidation protocol is further defined in [PMID: 30476874]. The proteins were digested in-solution without the use of reduction and alkylation using a two-step digestion approach (LysC, Trypsin) previously described [PMID: 30237127].  LC-MS/MS: 1 µg peptide mixture was separated on a two-column system on the EASY-nLC 1000 instrument (Termo Fisher Scientific). The system is comprised of two in-house fused silica columns; a precolumn (5 µm particle size, C18 beads, 4 cm × 100 µm ID) coupled to a laser-pulled analytical column (3 µm particle size, C18 beads, 20 cm × 75 µm ID). The peptides were separated at a flow rate of 250 nL/min over a 60 mins gradient from 5-38% solution B (90% ACN, 0.1 % FA). Reverse phase separated peptides were subsequently analysed on QExactive HF Quadrupole-Orbitrap (Thermo Fisher Scientific) mass spectrometer in positive ion mode using data-dependent acquisition. Full scans were performed across a range of 400-1400 m/z and recorded with 120,000 resolution.  AGC target was set 3 x10^6 with a maximum injection time on 100ms. The MS/MS scan mode selected top 12 most intense ions with a charge-state +2-+4. Resolution was set to 15,000 with an AGC target of 1 x 10^5 and maximum injection time of 50 ms. HCD collision energy set to 28 and a dynamic exclusion of 5s.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw MS data were acquired and processed using Xcalibur (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Data files were analysed using Progenesis QI (nonlinear Dynamics, USA) for chromatographic alignment, grouped according to their conditions, and precursor peak quantification. Data searches were carried out using Proteome Discoverer 2.1 and search against an isoform database of Murine Laminin (downloaded 18 January 2017) For MPO-mediated oxidation, MPO isoform sequences were included in the database (updated 6th June 2017)  The following search parameters were used: parent ion tolerance - 4 ppm; fragment ion tolerance - 0.1 Da; trypsin - 2 missed cleavages allowed; fixed modifications – none; variable modifications: Chlorination (Y, W), 2 x Chlorination (Y, W), 1 x oxidation (M, H, C, W), 2 x oxidations  (M, C, W), and 3 x oxidations (C). All other parameters were left as default.
